lens.title: Intraocular lenses
lens.lead: Three materials, one manufacturing standard. Every EyeKon lens is lathe-cut and inspected in Clearwater, Florida.
lens.hl.name: Hydrophilic acrylic IOLs
lens.hl.d: A proprietary copolymer of hydrophilic and hydrophobic monomers that behaves like the natural crystalline lens — excellent folding and biocompatibility. Every lens is screened with our Clear View process for unpolymerized material.
lens.hl.c1: Free of vacuoles and glistening; does not stick to instruments
lens.hl.c2: Square-edge design to reduce posterior capsule opacification
lens.hl.c3: Co-aspheric optics across the whole range
lens.hl.ny: Natural Yellow (NY) versions filter UVA and violet light using 3-hydroxykynurenine, the same chromophore found in the young human lens.
lens.yellowkey: Blue dot: clear version · Yellow dot: Natural Yellow version.
lens.hb.name: Hydrophobic IOLs
lens.hb.d: Lathe-cut — not molded — hydrophobic acrylic with a high refractive index, for a thinner lens, smaller incision and lower risk of PCO, inflammation and bacterial adhesion.
lens.hb.c1: Free of vacuoles and glistening thanks to lathe cutting
lens.hb.c2: Aspheric optic that offsets the eye's positive spherical aberration
lens.pm.name: PMMA IOLs
lens.pm.d: Time-tested PMMA-CQ UV, the material used since the very first intraocular lens in 1949. Lathe-cut from buttons or rods in one-piece and three-piece designs.
lens.pm.c2: Excellent tissue tolerance and long-term stability
lens.pm.c3: The most cost-effective option for high-volume programs
lens.aconst.note: A-constants are estimates. Each surgeon is encouraged to personalize their own. Anterior chamber and premium lenses are not for sale in the US.
lens.pl.d: A disposable, front-loaded cartridge and injector system that arrives ready to use: fewer steps in the OR and less handling of the lens.

pat.title: Cataract surgery, explained simply
pat.lead: Cataract surgery is one of the most common and successful operations in the world. Here is what you should know.
pat.q1.title: What is a cataract?
pat.q1.p1: Inside your eye there is a natural lens that focuses light. With age it slowly becomes cloudy and yellowish: that is a cataract.
pat.q1.p2: It happens to almost everyone eventually. It is not an illness you caused, and it can be treated.
pat.q1.c2: Colors that look faded or yellow
pat.q1.c3: Glare and halos around lights at night
pat.q1.imgalt: Simulation of vision with a cataract compared with vision after surgery
pat.q2.title: How does the surgery work?
pat.q2.lead: The cloudy lens is replaced by a clear artificial lens, called an intraocular lens (IOL). It stays in your eye for life.
pat.s1.d: Your surgeon measures your eye and helps you choose the right lens for your lifestyle.
pat.s2.d: An outpatient procedure, usually under 30 minutes, with local anesthesia. You go home the same day.
pat.s3.d: Most people notice clearer vision within days. Follow your surgeon's drops and check-ups.
pat.q3.title: Which lens is right for me?
pat.q3.lead: There is no single best lens — only the best lens for how you live. Talk about it with your surgeon.
pat.l1.d: Sharp vision at one distance, usually far. You may need glasses for reading.
pat.l2.d: Good vision from far to intermediate — computer, cooking, dashboard.
pat.l3.d: Designed to move with the eye to help focus at different distances.
pat.l4.d: Filters part of the blue-violet light, like the natural lens of a young eye.
pat.sim.title: See it before you choose
pat.sim.lead: Ask your surgeon about IOLSIMULATOR: with a virtual reality headset you can preview how you would see with each lens.
pat.faq.title: Frequently asked questions
pat.f1.a: The eye is numbed with drops or local anesthesia. Most patients feel only light pressure.
pat.f2.q: How long does the lens last?
pat.f2.a: Intraocular lenses are designed to last a lifetime and do not need to be replaced.
pat.f3.q: Can both eyes be operated on at once?
pat.f3.a: Usually each eye is operated on separately, a few days or weeks apart. Your surgeon will decide.
pat.f4.a: It depends on the lens you choose. Many people need glasses only for certain tasks.
pat.f5.a: Rings or glow around lights at night. Some lens designs cause more than others — the simulator helps you see the difference.
pat.medical: This information is general and does not replace the advice of your eye surgeon.
